questions.question:
**Direction: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

The coach said / that Shreyas / had practicing on / the lawn tennis court.
questions.solution:
Here, the erroneous part is **'had practicing on.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct phrase is** 'had been practicing'** instead of **'had practicing.'**
 
• The error is in the verb tense as** 'had practicing'** is not a grammatically correct form.
 
• In past perfect continuous tense, we use **"had been"** followed by the **base form of the verb + "ing".**
 
• So, **"had been practicing" **is the correct form in this context.
 
• The sentence should read as *'The coach said that Shreyas **had been practicing on**__ the lawn tennis court.'*
 
• The correct answer is Option 4.

 __

• The correct option, **"want to surrender",** accurately reflects the meaning of the idiom.
 
• The correct answer is Option 4.

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

The melodious song reminded Revathi **__on the nostalgic moments of__** her past.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"of the nostalgic moments of."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The presence of the word **"on"** is incorrect.
 
• **"On"** can indicate the subject of an action or event.
 
 
• **Example**: *He congratulated her on her success.*
 
 
 
• The preposition **"of"** is used to show possession or association, making it the most appropriate option for the sentence.
 
• In this corrected sentence, the preposition **"of" **is used after the verb **"reminded"** to indicate what the song reminded Revathi of.
 
• The correct answer is Option 4.

 

**Correct sentence**: *The melodious song reminded Revathi **of the nostalgic moments of**__ her past.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1, "by the nostalgic moments in"**, suggests that the song was reminding Revathi of something happening during her past nostalgic moments, rather than the nostalgic moments themselves.
 
• **Option 2, "at the nostalgic moments of",** is grammatically incorrect as "at" cannot be used with "nostalgic moments of".
 
• **Option 3, "of the nostalgic moments at",** is also grammatically incorrect as "at" cannot be used with "nostalgic moments of".

questions.solution:

• The idiom** "It takes two to tango" **means that both parties involved in a situation are responsible for the outcome. (किसी स्थिति में शामिल दोनों पक्ष परिणाम के लिए जिम्मेदार होते हैं)

• The phrase is often used to suggest that someone is unfairly blaming one person for a problem that was caused by both parties.
 
• The origin of the phrase is from the dance, the Tango, which requires two people to dance together.
 
• The correct answer is Option 2.
